chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated with this sanad from Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Miskān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān: the like of the hadith of al-Naḍr. He said:
The Shaykh, may Allah Exalted support him, said:

The person performing tayammum may pray with his tayammum all the prayers of the night and day, both obligatory and supererogatory, so long as he does not do anything that invalidates taharah or become able to use water. فإذا he becomes able to use it, his tayammum is invalidated, and purification with it becomes obligatory for him for salat (prayer). If he is negligent in that until the water is no longer available to him and he reaches a state in which the use of water harms him, he repeats the tayammum.

What indicates that is His saying, Exalted is He, in the verse of purification, and that He, Exalted is He, made purification obligatory upon one standing for salat (prayer) when he finds water, then joined to it tayammum when water is absent. Salat is a generic noun, so it is as though He said: purification suffices you for the genus of salat (prayer) when you find water, and when you do not find it, tayammum suffices you for its genus. So just as purification is not restricted to a single prayer, likewise tayammum is not restricted.

If it is said: His saying, Exalted is He, indicates the obligation of purification or tayammum, if water is not present, upon everyone rising for salat (prayer), and this requires the obligation of tayammum for every prayer. We say: the apparent sense of the command does not indicate repetition, so it does not indicate more than a single act. Thus the repetition of purification and tayammum is not obligatory by the repetition of rising. Do you not see that you hold that if a man were to say to his wife, 'You are divorced when you enter the house,' his statement would not entail more than one occurrence in your view, and if her entering were repeated, the occurrence of divorce upon her would not be repeated. And this is also indicated by...

key_terms.اسْتِعْمَالِ الْمَاءِ: the use of water for purification
key_terms.التَّكْرَارِ: repetition, here in the legal sense of whether the command must be repeated
key_terms.تَيَمُّمِهِ: his tayammum, the dry ablution used in place of water purification

ai.seo_question: Does tayammum suffice for more than one salat (prayer), or must it be renewed for every prayer?
ai.summary: This text presents a legal ruling that tayammum remains valid for multiple obligatory and supererogatory prayers so long as nothing occurs to invalidate taharah and water does not become available. It also argues from the Qur’anic purification verse that the command does not inherently imply repetition for every single salat (prayer), making tayammum analogous to wudu in covering the genus of prayer until invalidated.
